claims.claim: The great frost: from October a great cold; the sea froze "ad centum millia" out from the northern coasts of the Pontus; in February of the second indiction the ice broke "in multa ac varia ſrusta ... speciem referentia disrupta est", was driven by the winds through the mouth of the Pontus to the city; "eujus de visu tesles exstitimus"; "unum quippe illius ſragmentum quasi triginta ... ejusdem juvenes ludibundi a>cendimus" (scan: "a>cendimus")

The Life names no author; its writer took up the praise "adhortatione adductus", with "multorum" displaced by the scan to l.802
Father Isaac (Isaacius) and mother Theodota, rich; father died "cum jam puer ... irimulus esset" (trimulus; the scan sets a column letter between); a gap follows ("Mater autem. . .")
Home city: "illa patria, quz imperii dignitate decorata", unnamed
Wedding night: he spoke to his bride of the shortness of life; she agreed; they lived the monastic life within the world
Father-in-law angered the emperor; "Leo hic ſuit Copronymi filius"; threatened "oculos effossurum"; sent to Cyzicus; met Gregory at Sigriane
Leo IV: "Leone quarto Constantini F."
"Nondum anni tres przterierant" when father-in-law and emperor died; Irene ruled with her son
Wealth given to the poor; she in the monastery "in insula Principe"; he to Strategios at Sigriane, monastery Polychronius, tonsured
Monastery built on the paternal estate on Calonymus; copied sacred books ("Divinorum librorum seriptioni assidue incumbebat")
Sigriane mountain: bought from a farmer a plot "jam agri nomen erm" (erat); others took him as guide ("eorumque. præſectum agebat")
Nicaea: "Cum enim Nicææ synodus secundo coacta esset" he went "solito cilicino saeco indutus, 3C asine insidens" (sacco, ac asinæ); "strenue propugnata veriiate"
The council at Nicaea met in 787
Leo "scelestissimum hominem", of Armenian and Assyrian descent; drove out "Ecclesize solem ejicit" and nearly all bishops; attacked the images of Christ, his Mother and the saints
Genesios: Leo condemned "summum sacerdotem Nicephorum" to exile; Theophanes on a shore with candles and incense; "Ad sanctum, inquit , Patrem atque confessorem Theophanem monasterii Agriensis"

Debate: Life unnamed man versed in sorcery; notice names "Joanni ariolo"; notice: threatened with the gallows
Held in the Eleutherius palace; "Duos igitur annos acerbissimo defunctus carcere"; to Samothrace; died after "tres supre viginti une dies" (supra ... unde)
818, Leo's fifth year, against Baronius; prison from 816

Goar: Baronius split Theophanes into two

Combefis: later Greek and Latin breviaries mostly reproduced Theophanes
Continuation begins with Leo the Armenian, where Theophanes ends; written by order of Constantine Porphyrogenitus
Catalogue of Theodore the Studite's letters (titles and opening words, Coislin 94): letter 411 to Theophanes "prxposito" of Agros (Greek garbled), letter 476 "Theophani præposito et conſessori"

claims.claim: The coin: on his way in he asked a devout man for a coin, "a pio aliquo viro nummum petiit ei accepit, quem quidem intra cucullam geslabat"; held it up: "Cujus est, o imperator, imago hec et auperscriptio?"; Constantine: "Imperatorum"; if thrown down and trodden, punished? those standing by: "Omnino"; then what of one who tramples Christ and his mother in an image; "nummum projecit et calcavit"
claims.witness: PG100 Vita Stephani l.95528-95537 (Phiale, Pharos, the coin), l.95695-95732

claims.claim: Constantine V's campaign against the images; the Life calls the iconoclasts Iconocaustae

Life by Stephen the Deacon of the church of Constantinople; Fabricius: written 808; Stephen killed 766; Benedictines: written in the 42nd year after the death "ut auctor ipse teslatur"; the author: 42 years have passed, gathered from "viris veridicis ejusque discipulis"

Benedictines: Metaphrastes drew his Life from it; the author took phrases and whole sentences from Cyril's Life of Euthymius; the Life tells much of the history of the iconoclasts clearly ("pleraque ad historiam leonoclastarum spectantia", "luculenter enarrantur")
Ages: tonsured "ætatis annum decimum sextum agentem" under John on Auxentius; enclosed "2tatis anno tricesimo primo"; to the summit at 42

Born in Constantinople; parents' story set in the first year of Artemius-Anastasius, year of the world 6202 in Loppin's Latin, bracket "[Christi anno 713]"; mother Anna prayed at the Blachernae icon; conceived when Germanus became patriarch; baptized by Germanus
The council of 754 against the images (Percival/Hefele: Hieria, then Blachernae); in the Life the council held in the Blachernae church, then all sign

Callistus the patrician sent up the mountain to have him sign "synodi deſinitioni"; Stephen: "ego Stephanus neque subseribo"; cupped hand: "Etiamsi tantulum vitalis sanguinis mihi esset, pro Christi imagine effundatur"; sends back the food

Carried down by two men, unable to stand from fasting; bishops (Theodosius of Ephesus, Constantine of Nicomedia, Constantine of Nakoleia and others) at the Chrysopolis monastery; Callistus: "Vieti sumus, imperator, victi sumus"; exiled to Proconnesus

Back from Proconnesus to the Phiale prison, then after the coin to the Praetorium; there 342 monks ("ad trecentos quadraginla duos"), noses cut off, eyes dug out, hands cut off, for refusing to sign against the images

Eleven months in the Praetorium; the emperor rises at the second hour, rushes out "in imperatoria vestibula exsiliens" and meets revellers going to the feast in the empress's honor; he: "Non sum ego imperator. Alius vester imperator est ... Stephanus Auxentii"; a crowd runs to the prison; "Ego sum, quem quzritis"; ropes tied between the chains on his feet; dragged into the public street; Philomates kills him with a pole from the fire siphons; body thrown into the pit of pagans and the condemned, "ubi uimirum saneti martyris Pelagii" "lemplum olim erat, quod cum lapsum"; Constantine had made the ruin a tomb of the condemned ("pulcrum effecit, Pelagiique titulo insignivit")
Death: "quinquagesimo tertio su ætatis anno, mense ... die vigesima Octava"
Variant at the death: "Regius Codex non habet tptrty" (τρίτῳ, third, garbled; so his fiftieth year)

Theophanes: 20 November, indiction 4 (Goar's margin A.C. 757); "Stephanum juniorem protomartyrem inclusum ad sanctum Auxentium"; accused "quod plerosque ad monasticam vitam esset hortatus, et aulæ dignitates divitiasque contemnere suasisset"; one foot tied with a rope; dragged by scholarii and soldiers from the Praetorium to Pelagius and torn apart; "annos sexaginta in clausura exegil"; officials and soldiers punished for images

Nikephoros's Short History (marked "An. 766"): a holy monk shut in a narrow hut at the foot of the mountain of Saint Auxentius, accused of drawing people from homes, kin and palaces to the monastic life; beaten, imprisoned, a rope tied to his feet, dragged from the palace to the Forum of the Ox and torn apart; body thrown to Pelagius's tombs, where pagans' and executed men's bodies went
Patrologia Graeca editors of Theophanes: Theophanes runs together events of several years; dragged from his hut 763, Proconnesus 766, martyred 767 on 28 November, not after sixty years in enclosure

In the Life Stephen the Younger tells the monks John of Damascus "quem hic tyrannus Mansur nominabat, nos autem sanctum et deiferum appellamus" kept writing against the emperor (agrees with batch 9's John of Damascus record)
Theodore gathers the broken skull pieces; the abbot of Dios lays them in a box within the altar; Theodore exiled to Sicily with wife and children
Fiery cloud over the mountain he came from, hail on the city, while he was dragged

claims.claim: Crowning: as he set the crown on Leo's head, "quasi in spinas et iribulos mannin injicere"; "palam proſitebatur ingenti se doloris sensu affectuin esse"; in the church "quod a Sapientia nomen habet"
Theophanes: Leo crowned "in Magnæ ecclesiz ambone a Nicephoro patriarcha" on 11 July, indiction 6; the Bollandists: "ergo anno 813"

Goar: Leo, crowned by Nikephoros ("Nicephoro diadema capiti imponente"), seized power "anno Christi 814, Junii die 42, indictione septima, prout Baronius" and an anonymous Greek chronicle say, differing from Theophanes (the scan's day 42 cannot stand)
Goar: exiled when Leo's second year was complete ("Imperii anno secundo jam completo"), at the end of Lent 816: "Ad quadragesimz ſinem anno 816 indict. 9 Nicephoro tendit insidias, et sede abdicat"
Ignatius: Leo put off signing the creed until crowned, then on the second day refused ("Is se ſacturum fortiter pernegat")
Theophanes: before entering the city Leo wrote to Nikephoros, "quem de reela sua in Deum fide certiorem fecit"

Fabricius: patriarch in place of Tarasius 806, 12 April, Easter; deposed 815 for the images; "homologeta, sive eonſessor, Græeis dictus"; died in a monastery 828; Life by Ignatius, deacon of Constantinople
Bollandists: born "circa annum 758"; ordained 12 April, Easter, 806; exiled 13 March 815; died in the 14th year of exile, 2 June 828; body brought back 846
Bollandists' note to the Life of Methodios: "Sanctus Nicephornus in exsilium pulsus est" "anno 814 die 13 Martii"

Goar, preface to Nikephoros's short chronology: Baronius has him die "anno nimirum 806 ad 828, hoc postremo mortuum" "scribit, qui tamen sequentis 829 mensem Junium" (attigit); the preface compares the editions of Camerarius, Contius and Scaliger, which the edition's own preface names as the basis of Goar's text of 1652

Ignatius, deacon and keeper of the vessels of the Great Church, later metropolitan of Nicaea (Suidas), wrote the Lives of Tarasius and Nikephoros; calls Nikephoros his father and himself his son; deplores his own lapse into heresy
Ignatius's own confession in the Life: he was polluted by the accursed communion and asks help to expiate the heresy

Combefis: Ignatius "aliquando vim passum et hereticis imaginum effractoribus communicasse"; wrote "pœnitudine ductus" when Methodius was installed; Combefis translated the Greek ("Græca Ignatii ... reddidi")

Father Theodore, an imperial secretary under Constantine V, flogged, stripped of rank, exiled to Pemolina, recalled, tortured again, exiled to Nicaea and died there; mother Eudocia followed him in exiles
Nikephoros chosen scribe "a secretis" to the emperors
At the council of 787 under Tarasius, among the officials, he proclaimed the veneration of images, a confessor "etiam ante sacras infulas"; Mai: he attended and spoke, as Ignatius and the acts say
Left the court for a cave "e regione Bosphori Thracii" on a barren height and built a monastery; later curator of the great poorhouse
Chosen as layman by the emperor's urging; became a monk at his own request; consecrated at the Easter feast

Theophanes: elected 12 April, Easter, by people, priests and emperors; "Plato autem et Theodorus, Studii monasterii superior, Nicephori ordinationi non assenserunt", since a layman should not leap to the top; the emperor Nikephoros wished to drive them from the city; Theophanes: not new, many laymen made bishops

Sirmond chronology: a synod called by the emperor Nikephoros restored the steward Joseph "utennque consentiente novo patriarcha", inexperienced and fearing the emperor; Plato, Theodore and Joseph of Thessalonica abstained from Nikephoros's communion over Joseph; peace under Michael I in 811

Theophanes: Theodore, his brother Joseph of Thessalonica and Plato separated from Nikephoros's communion over Joseph the steward, who had crowned Constantine and Theodote illegally; the emperor's synod exiled them in January
Goar: Nikephoros restored Joseph "ut imperatoris gratiam iniret"

Leo orders a debate with the iconoclasts; Nikephoros answers: Alexandria, Antioch, Jerusalem do not agree, no Roman priest, no catholic synod; "optimus sit imperator, qui ex bello pacem componere possit" and you have brought war on a settled church

Night exile: a patrician with soldiers sent "media nocte Dominice lucis"; ill, he rises with a servant's help, censes, lights two candles in the catechumenium where he often prayed all night, lies prone, prays, then is carried on a litter; boat to the monastery "Boni nomine", then to the farther monastery of the martyr Theodore, both his foundations
Theophanes the priest: fourteen years in exile; buried in the monastery he founded
Michael II "fertur respondisse": let Tarasius's synod and those under Constantine and Leo be set aside; he may come and preside if he says nothing about the images; Nikephoros holds to his confession
Antirrheticus I: "omni ævo auditum est corpus incircumscriptum ?"; to say a body is not circumscribed is to say it is not in a place, and what is not in a place is not a body
claims.witness: PG100 Antirrheticus I, Mai's Latin, l.17809-17816

claims.claim: Mai: Antirrhetici written in exile after the larger Apologeticus of 817; died 828 "septuageuarius"; aimed at Constantine by name and at Leo V; they recite segments of a "libri bactenus incogniti Iconomachorum, Copronymi regio nomine et auctoritate 8cripti"; Banduri: surpassed the bishops of Constantinople since Chrysostom
Mai: Leo V, whom Nikephoros as patriarch had crowned "au. 813, coronaverat"
Mai's note: Mamonas is Constantine V
Breviarium: from Maurice's death 602 to Leo IV and Irene's marriage, 770; Photius cod. 66 read and praised it
Photius, Bibliotheca codex 66: "Read the Historical Epitome of Nicephorus patriarch of Constantinople."; "he throws into the shade all historians who have preceded him"
Death: last words "Benedictus Deus, qui non dedit nos in captionem dentibus eorum"
Translation: Methodius opened the tomb; body "undeviginti annorum spatio integrum"; laid in the Holy Apostles "tertio Idus Martii", the day of his exile
Theophanes the priest is another and younger man than Theophanes the Confessor (Bollandists)
Theodore the Studite's letter to him in exile: "Salve, magne sol doctrine orthodoxæ"; the Bollandists call Theodore "Familiaris"
Sirmond chronology: after Theodotos was intruded, Theodore wrote for the abbots that, bound to Nikephoros as head, they could not attend the synod without him
Roman Martyrology: "paternarum traditionum propugnator acerrimus", fourteen years of exile; feasts 13 March and 2 June
Short History tells Stephen the Younger's death

Mediis aulem in epulis, uti habebamus, in navem nos impo-"; no garment, bedding, book or comforter allowed, "ea ceptis duobus homuncionibus iilite ratis"; "Hiemis rigorem"; "Enses enim et arcus ei clypei"; "super palea, omni stragula destitutus"
The banquet yearly: "quotannis in beati Tryphonis fefto moris" (the Latin version printed in Mansi)

1 February; by boat from the Boukoleon to Hieria; on foot to Galakrenai in deep snow: "Vocalo itaque Nicolas patriarcha prima Februarii"; "lintri imponentes in Hieriam"; "agre pedes ad Galacrenos usque pre nivium nimia copia venit"

claims.claim: Year of the exile 907: "so ergiebt sich als Datum des Exils des Nicolaus der 1. Febr. 907"; against 908 "wie Krug und Muralt nach Symeon Magister annehmen"
Mystikos: "officium mystici gesserat (quod ei cognominis instar"; Henschen: "Constantinopolitani mysticus fuerat S. Nicolaus", of the emperor's secret council
claims.witness: PG111, Mai's Monitum l.668-669; Henschen's Notitia l.326-328

claims.claim: Nicolaus Priscus, the first of the name: "idem Nicolaus Priscus, seu cjus nominis primus"
Three wives dead, fourth on the pretext of the infant: "cum per trium uxorum mortem"; "quartam uxorem ducere in animum induxit"; "præ- textu sane infantis quem ex illo pepererat"
Constantine born in 905: "Da Constantin sicher a. 905 geboren ist"
The Eastern church forbids fourth marriages: "universa ſere Orien- talis Eeelesia quartis nuptiis interdieit"
claims.witness: PG111, Mai l.872-873; Letter 32 l.13791-13794 ("de divinorum cano- num prohibitione")

claims.claim: Bishops refuse baptism unless Leo promises to dismiss the woman; he swears; within three days she is received with a wife's honors: "Placuerat enim archiepiscopis et sacerdoti - bus denegare baptismum infantis"; "jurejurando interposito allirmat, se repudiasse uxorem"; "Nondum 4ertio elapso die a baptismo"
Nicholas: Leo crowned her himself: "enim conjugi coronam imposuit, neque nobis, neque ullo de sacerdotibus"; "tanquam sponsus et sacerdos"
claims.witness: PG111, Letter 32, l.14009-14018 (a column mark 'C' at l.14014)

claims.claim: Chronicles: blessing by the priest Thomas, deposed for it; Zoe proclaimed Augusta; Leo barred from church, entering by the right side: "Benedictionem $2cro nuptiarum ritu cum Zoe uxore consecutus Leo a Thoma presbytero"; "benedictionem nuptialem a Thoma presbytero"; "qui eam pb rem officio depositus est"; "clesiæ ingressu Leoni interdixit"
Baptism at Epiphany by Nicholas, Alexander and Samonas sponsors; comet at the birth: "Inſantem baptizavit"; "susceptoribus ex saero ſonte Alexaudro"
Nicholas falls at Leo's feet; the unwritten-law plea: "ad genua, imo ad pedes provolutus"; "dicitur esse lex non scripta, haud ut legem violet"; "debet legi scripte"

His proposal and Leo's refusal: "O rex et fili"; "Conjux privatim degat neque cum tua majeslate commoretur"; "veteris Romz aliarumque pontiſicalium sedium præsules"; "sed ne unum quidem diem ab illa velle separari"
Letter 32 written in 912 to win the pope over: "Dieser Brief, geschrieben a. 912 bald nach der Wiederein- setzung des Nicolaus"
The Life speaks for the opposing party: "während hier ein Vertreter der Gegen- partei zu Worte kommt"; "wir es mit einer Parteischrift zu thun haben"

Author a monk of Euthymius's Psamathia monastery, a contemporary; written no earlier than 921: "zu den Mönchen des von Euthymius gegründeten und regierten Psamathias-Klosters"; "als frühester Termin lässt sich vielmehr das Jahr 921 festsetzen"

The Life's treason charge: a letter in Nicholas's hand to Andronicus Dux; then the baptism against his metropolitans: "eigenhändiges Schreiben des Patriarchen Nicolaus hochverräthe- rischen Inhalts"; "trotz des Widerspruchs seiner Metropoliten"

De Boor's judgment: "Ein absolut zwingender Beweis für die Schuld des Nico- laus ist nun allerdings nicht zu erbringen"; "dass die Anklage unseres Autors gegen Nicolaus berechtigt ist"; "dem Sinne nach, einen wirklichen Brief"
claims.witness: DEBOOR l.8776-8780, l.9277-9281; he sets the question of genuine or forged aside at l.6060-6062

claims.claim: Offers to readmit the banned emperor (1 May, 6 August 906) and refusals (25 December 906, 6 January 907), by the Life's feasts as de Boor dates them: "Nicolaus bietet dem gebannten Kaiser"; "Der Patriarch verweigert dein Kaiser den"; "Weihnachten, Epiphanias) fallen unzweifelhaft in die unmittelbar vorhergehende Zeit a. 906—907"
claims.witness: DEBOOR l.6033-6035, l.6611-6616 (the table's years read 000 in the scan), l.9246-9248

claims.claim: Legates of Rome side with Leo and allow the marriage: the Romans "exsilio nostro ealculum ad- jecerunt"; Mai: Sergius III "dispensationem ad quartas nuptias Leoni con- ces8erat", and the Roman Church "in causa nuptiarum missis etiam legatis ſaverat"

Legates of the eastern patriarchs also allow the marriage: Eutychius "Scripsit ergo Leo imperator ad patriarcham", "matrimo- nium ipsi licitum pronuntiarunt"; de Boor on the Life "dass alle Patri- archen willig seien, dem Kaiser den Dispens für seine Ehe zu ertheilen"; de Boor holds their presence proved against those who doubted it ("ist bisher be- zweifelt")

Restoration after Leo's death; Euthymius deposed: "miss0que ad Nicolaun ad Galacrenas nuntio, Euthymium patriarcham deposuit, et Nicolaum secundo restitnit"; "mittens Alexander Nicolaum ex Galacrenis tulit"
claims.witness: PG111, Henschen quoting Leo the Grammarian, l.456-460; PG109 l.65965-65980

claims.claim: Recalled by Leo (his own letters) or by Alexander (the chroniclers): "ob be- reits durch Leo, wie er selbst in seinen Briefen berichtet oder"; "durch Alexander, wie die Chronisten angehen"

Guardian for Constantine: Alexander dying named Nicholas, Stephen the magister and others "procuratoribus institutis"; "Nicolaus patriar- cha rebus communibus providebat"; Mai: "Nicolaus pracipuus regii pueri tutor"
claims.witness: PG111, Henschen quoting Leo the Grammarian, l.471-530; Mai l.806-808

claims.claim: Letter 10 to Symeon: "fili mi, si tamen filium nominare oportet, qui patrem injuria allicit; pater tamen tibi"; "est, velis nolis, episcopus, quanquam minimus, qui"; "in Deum pietatem non negavit"

Symeon at war at the walls; 26 letters; Nicholas himself as envoy: "prolizæ ad Simeonem principem Bulgarorum epistolæ viginti sex"; "Cum ergo mœnia ipsa Constantinopoleos Bulgarorum arma"; "ipse postremo legatus accedens (epist. 27, 50)"
Born 852; 73 years at death; died 15 May 925: "(geb. a. 852)"; "wurde er 73 Jahre"

Patriarch in 895 (Henschen, Mai) or 1 March 901 (de Boor): "provectus est anno 895"; "Nicolaus nosler sub Leone Sapiente imp. ad patriarchalem sedem evertus Fuit anno 895"; "statt, welcher im Jahre 901 auf den 1. März fiel"

Death 15 May 925 (Henschen) or 924 (Mai); buried in his monastery at Galakrenai; 13 or 14 years in the second term: "Mortuus ergo est $anetus Nicolaus 15"; "donec anno 924"; "annos tredecim : ejusque corpus in Gala- crenarum monasterio ab co condito"; "potitus annos quatuordeeim"

Leo's death and the return in 911 (Henschen, Mai) or 912 (de Boor): "Annus is erat nongentesimus undect- mus"; "quam nonnisi anno 911 sub Alexandro"; "Restitutus autem in sede ab Alexan- dro imperatore, anno 911, aut initio sequentis"; "am 12. Mai 912 erfolgten Tode des Kaisers Leo"

The Tomus of Union: Constantine convokes Nicholas and the bishops; pardon for Leo after death; fourth marriages banned; year 6428, indiction 8: "Nicolao patriarcha, cum univerfo pontificum cce-"; "que {uo etiam poft mortem communi decreto de-"; "indi@ionis octave, quartas nuptias ullus contra-"; "anno Mundano VIM. CDXXVIII. Indi@ione VIII"
The account before the Tomus says Leo expelled him as a liar who swore and changed his mind: "expellit, ut mendacem, & qui multoties quidem"; "bus animum mutaffet remque data opera extra-"
Concord of the church in July, under Romanus: "lotius Eeclesiæ a Romano inita est concordia"; "qui a Nicolai et En- thymii partibus divisis steterant animis"
claims.witness: PG111, Henschen quoting Leo the Grammarian, l.544-548

claims.claim: Union dated 921 by de Boor: "auf die a. 921 erfolgte Verstän- digung, die ihren Ausdruck in dem sogenannten Tomus Unionis"
163 letters found in a Vatican codex, in seven classes: "Has invenimus centum et sexaginta tres in codice Vaticano"
Letter 32's pope: "vel sub Landone pontifice, ut putat Baronius, vel sub Anastasio lertio, ut censet Pagius"
Homily on Thessalonica, 904, the ninth year of his patriarchate; fragment only: "anno Christi 904 contigit (qui erat pontiſicatus Nicolai annus nonus)"; "tenuem tantummodo particulam hic reeitabo"

Ephraim (via Mai): monk, pious, wise; of Italian birth; eloquent: "gente ltalus, et a natura comparatus ad eloquentiam"; Mai on his holiness: "pastoralis insuper ejusdem zelus, constantia ct eximia charitas"
Henschen: feast 15 May in an old synaxary of Constantinople; 14 and 16 May elsewhere: "pervetusto Synaxario"; "ad diem sequentem 16 Maii"; "14 Maii"

Henschen on Leo the Grammarian "auctor coxvus"; Combefis reads the codex's closing note as showing him near the times he wrote of ("Fuisse eum supparem illis quorum res gestas prosecutus est, ipsa sub- scriptio clare indicat"); the note dates the chronicle's completion ("Absoluta est recentiorum imperato- rum Chronographia") to the year of the world 6521: "anno a mundo condilo sexmillesimo sexcente- simo vicesimo primo"
The Continuator depends on the Vatican recension of the Logothete: "der von ihr abhängige Continnator des Theophancs"

De Boor: Nicholas confused the wedding blessing and the crowning; crowning by the emperor after the patriarch blesses the diadem: "zwei verschiedene Handlungen verwirrt hat"; "Die Krönung pflegte stets vom Kaiser selbst vollzogen zu werden"; the Life confirms the priest: "und diese wird durch unsere Biographie bestätigt"

Legates' arrival: Nicholas eight or nine months after the wedding ("Octavo vel nono mense post initas illas nuptias"); the Life not yet arrived at the exile ("die Legaten als noch nicht eingetroffen"); de Boor sides with the Life ("diese sprechen für unseren Autor")
Eastern legates attested by Eutychius, Arethas and Leo Choerosphactes's letters: "der Anwesenheit orientalischer Legaten in Byzauz"
Abdication: "Nicolaus eine Abdankungsurkunde ausstellte" (Arethas: "sacri sui honoris repudii libellurn")
Modern writers built on the letter and praise him: "auch von gegnerischer Seite, gepriesen als das Muster eines Hirten"

Eutychius of Alexandria: Nicholas forbade another wife to Leo as a consecrated reader ("siquſdem ana- gnostes es et precibus sacerdotum consecratus"); legates and bishops pronounced it lawful; the son born after; Nicholas's successor named Anthimus

contested_claims.claim: Who blessed and crowned at the marriage
sides: Nicholas: Leo crowned Zoe himself, as bridegroom and priest, with no priest present (PG111 l.14009-14018)
Leo the Grammarian and Theophanes Continuatus: the priest Thomas gave the nuptial blessing and was deposed (PG108 l.99398-99400; PG109 l.33529-33531); de Boor says the Life confirms the priest
De Boor: Nicholas confused the blessing with Zoe's crowning, which the emperor performed (DEBOOR l.8411-8423)

contested_claims.claim: The treason charge (a letter to Andronicus Dux)
sides: The Life of Euthymius, a partisan work: true, and it explains Nicholas's conduct (DEBOOR l.6041-6058); the account before the Tomus of Union: expelled as a liar who often swore and changed his mind (MANSI l.103225-103238)

De Boor: true in substance with the greatest probability, though no compelling proof (DEBOOR l.8776-8780, l.9277-9281); at l.6060-6062 he sets aside whether the letter was genuine or forged by enemies
Nicholas's own Letter 32 never mentions it and blames Leo's desire and bribery of the bishops (PG111 l.14385-14389)
Nicholas: eight or nine months after the wedding, before his arrest (PG111 l.14277-14279)
The Life, as de Boor reads it: not yet arrived on the day of his exile; de Boor prefers the Life (DEBOOR l.8546-8561, l.8599-8611)
The Life and Arethas of Caesarea: he signed a written abdication (DEBOOR l.8837-8851, l.6427-6431)
Nicholas: seized and exiled (PG111 l.14390-14402)
His own letters, as de Boor reports: Leo (DEBOOR l.6479-6480)
The chronicles: Alexander (DEBOOR l.6498; PG109 l.65965; PG111 l.456-460)
895: Henschen (PG111 l.366) and Mai (PG111 l.662)
1 March 901: de Boor, from Fischer's patriarch lists and the Life (DEBOOR l.5362-5373, l.5803-5806)

contested_claims.claim: Year of Leo's death and Nicholas's return
sides: 911: Henschen, "anno 911, aut initio sequentis" (PG111 l.455-456, l.636-637); Mai (PG111 l.665)
912: de Boor (DEBOOR l.5220-5221)
15 May 925: Henschen (PG111 l.635-636); de Boor, from Fischer's lists (DEBOOR l.5343-5344)
Lando: Baronius, as Mai reports (PG111 l.863)
Anastasius III: Pagi, as Mai reports (PG111 l.863)
907: de Boor, from the patriarch lists (DEBOOR l.5362-5364, l.5797-5800)
908: Krug and Muralt, following Symeon Magister, as de Boor reports ("nicht, wie Krug und Muralt nach Symeon Magister annehmen, a.908", DEBOOR l.5798-5799)
Nine years after his election in 895, or eleven by Leunclavius: Mai ("post novennium (aut post annos XI, ut dicitur apud Leunclavium", PG111 l.662-664)

contested_claims.claim: Whether legates of the eastern patriarchs came
sides: De Boor: they came, on Eutychius, Arethas of Caesarea and the letters of Leo Choerosphactes (DEBOOR l.8640-8684)

The note Mansi prints before Nicholas's letter: the second synod that chose Euthymius is mentioned only by Eutychius, "cujus narrationem , quam ufquequaque veram pra- flare nolim" (MANSI l.93994-93998); de Boor names Mansi XVIII 242 among those who doubted the eastern legates (DEBOOR l.8646-8647, l.8656)

claims.claim: At Tephrike, on the embassy, Peter often talked with the Paulicians ("saepe et cum illis colloquerer"), learned more from "multis orthodoxis ibi degentibus", and heard them "garrientes" that they would send some of their own "in loca Bulgariae" to turn people from the right faith, since preaching there had only begun ("divina praedicatio ibi initium modo ceperit"), and that they could sow their "lolium" on the "latenti adhue vero tritico" (scan)

Tephrike a Paulician city on the eastern frontier: Karbeas "conderet Tibricam", wishing to be near "ab Armeniis et a Romania"; Rader: "Tibricam Armeniae civitatem"; the Paulicians a sect condemned and hunted by the empire (Theodora's commissioners), and an Armenian sect to John of Odzun
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), l.3757-3764; Rader l.601; TC (theophanes-continuatus_historiae-byzantinae-scriptores-post-theophanem-pg109-grc-lat_migne1863.txt) l.14936-14947; ODZUN (john-odzun_opera-arm-lat_aucher1834.txt) l.3913-3915, l.3826-3830

claims.claim: Sent "Imperatoris jussu ... ipso exordio imperii Basilii" for "captivorum permutatio"; again at the end: sent to exchange "duces captivos" (Greek ἄρχοντας αἰχμαλώτους), done "secundo anno imperii Basilii, et Constantini, et Leonis"; stayed "novem menses"
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), dedication l.787-795; close l.3826-3829 (Greek l.3800-3803)

claims.claim: Gieseler: Basil took power 24 September 867; the embassy "incidit in annum 868"; the History written at the emperor's order, before Chrysocheir's defeat and death "quae i» annum 871 incidit" (scan): "inter annes 868 et 871" (scan)

Gieseler: "Haec omnia sunt, quae de scriptore hujus libelli certo scimus"; Sicily "Petri nostri patria"; the flight from the Saracens, the language and lay status are conjectures ("conjicio autem, eum ad clerum non perfinuisse" (scan)), partly because a cleric would have given his rank at the letter's end
Gieseler: Peter belonged to the imperial court ("in aula Imperatoris, ad quam Petrus pertinuit"); found at Constantinople ("Petrum Siculum hoc tempore Constantinopoli invenimus")
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), Gieseler's note l.687-690; preface l.188

claims.claim: Done at the emperor's order: "divino mandato ipsorum sanctorum et orthodoxorum magnorum Imperato ... rum nostrorum ... obsecutus" (the word crosses a page break and footnote)

Dedicated "Archiepiscopo Bulgariae", the archbishop unnamed; signed "Antistiti Bulgariae Petrus"; Rader: "Archiepiscopo Bulgarorum nuper ad Christianam religionem traductorum"; Peter writes "incolumitatis multorum causa" and calls himself "in dicendo rudis"
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), title l.731-733; dedication l.742, l.840-848; Rader's observations l.620-621

claims.claim: Title: "de vana et futili haeresi Manichaeorum, qui Pauliciani etiam dicuntur"; Peter: "iidem sunt Pauliciani et Manichaei"

Peter's six marks: two principles, a bad God and a good, one maker and lord of this world, the other of the world to come; Mary scorned, Christ's body brought from heaven; the bread and wine of the sacrament refused; the cross insulted; the Old Testament and prophets rejected, with Peter's letters; "Presbyteros ab Ecclesia rejiciunt"
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), the six heads, l.1318-1325, l.1365-1382, l.1383-1421, l.1439-1446, l.1514-1517

claims.claim: Simple believers should not answer them but flee them "velut ab serpente"

Peter reports the Paulicians condemn "Manem et asseclas ejus ... praeterea Paulum. etiam Samosatenum promtissime dammant" (scan), and claim to have no part in the Manichaeans' "impuritatibus", though he says they keep their errors ("sunt tamen errorum illorum pertinaces custodes")
Gieseler: "Petrum falli, qui Paulicianos cum Manichaeis re vera eosdem esse contendat"

Gieseler: Photius's first book written while patriarch, before his first exile by Basil (the scan reads "067" for 867); Peter after 868; Peter used it "tecte", "Photii Imperatori invisi neque nomen neque libros laudare licuit", "idem saepe aliis verbis exprimeret"; Engelhardt "recte judicasse vidétur" (scan)
Peter on Mani copied Cyril of Jerusalem "prope syllabatim" (Rader); Gieseler marks the passage from Cyril's sixth Catechesis
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), Rader's observations l.680-684; Gieseler's note l.1552-1554

claims.claim: Peter's informants per Rader: "partim a Manichaeis, quibuscum disputando congressus erat, partim a Catholicis"
The History tells the line of teachers down to Sergius (Tychicus), and Karbeas, Chrysocheir ("consobrinus ipsius et gener")
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), l.668-671 (Rader), l.3015, l.3298, l.3743-3761, l.3825

claims.claim: Promised sequel: "de quibusdam autem ἀρυὰ cos perfectiorum haeresibus in sequentibus vobis exponetur, si Deus nobis vilibus coneesserit" (scan); Sirmond found in the Vatican "duorum tantum capitum refutationem ... ex nudis prope divinarum literarum testimoniis contextam"
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), close l.3857-3858; Gieseler l.376-379; Rader l.660-662

claims.claim: One Vatican manuscript; fragments first in Baronius's Annals in Sirmond's Latin; Baronius's tome IX calls him "Lucas Siculus"; Rader's edition Ingolstadt 1604

Rader: "A ureolum hunc libellum" (scan); Rader's dedication set "Manichaeos et Peulicianos cum Lutheranis, Calvinianis, Iconoclastis" (scan: Peulicianos), omitted by Gieseler as hardly any scholar would miss it
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), Rader's preface l.558; Gieseler l.540-544

claims.claim: Rader: Peter lived "praeter propter DCCCLXX"; the embassy "uno dumtaxat anno ?) ante VIII Synodum" (scan, with a footnote mark); Rader asks if he is the "Siculum Magistrum" of Skylitzes: "Suspicor omnino eundem"
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), Rader's observations l.599-603, l.609-611, l.629-630

claims.claim: Peter of Argos: the identification rests on Blanditius's Latin title of the funeral oration for Athanasius of Methone; the Greek names the bishop of Argos; Blanditius inserted "Siculi"; the Life of Peter of Argos makes him born at Constantinople. The scan lacks the page where this argument begins

The unnamed archbishop: Rader, the case still pending after Formosus was refused; Gieseler: "Haec omnia nihili esse", and his conjecture that no archbishop was yet chosen when Greek priests were sent after the council of 869; on that conjecture "Petrus seripsit intra annos 869 et 974" (scan; 974 a slip for 871)
claims.witness: PETER (peter-of-sicily_historia-manichaeorum-seu-paulicianorum-grc-lat_gieseler1846.txt), Rader l.620-652; Gieseler l.687-690, l.204-219

claims.claim: John of Odzun, Armenian catholicos (Aucher: raised to the patriarchal see "anno ^i8." (scan), synodal oration "anno 71g." (scan; the file header reads 719) "in?arbe Tvin" (scan)); his sermon against the Paulicians: they went from attacking images to attacking the cross; they call the orthodox idolaters for honoring the sign of the cross, and blame the painted image of the incarnate Word; canon 32 forbids dealing with "Pauliciani". No founder is named
claims.witness: ODZUN (john-odzun_opera-arm-lat_aucher1834.txt), Aucher's preface l.196, l.247-249; canon 32 l.3826-3830; sermon l.3900-3918, l.3978-3989; searched for constantin, sergi, silvan, tychic: none

claims.claim: Theophanes the Confessor: "Manichæos, qui nune Pauliciani" (scan) (under Michael I)

Theophanes Continuatus tells the persecution under Theodora, Karbeas's flight, the founding of Tephrike, Basil's campaign and Chrysocheir's death; no Paulician teaching and no mention of Peter's embassy
claims.witness: TC (theophanes-continuatus_historiae-byzantinae-scriptores-post-theophanem-pg109-grc-lat_migne1863.txt) l.14936-14968, l.15150-15152, l.24540-24600, l.25200-25317; searched permutat, commutat, captivorum

claims.claim: Rački: Peter as Basil's envoy at Tephrike "god. 868" heard of the plan for Bulgaria; "Neznamo, u koliko su tibrički Pavlićani bili izveli pomenutu osnovu glede Bugarske"; their teaching reached Bulgaria all the same; Photius wrote a few years before Peter
Gifford: "Petrus Siculus (circ. a.d. 870) who quotes the passage in his History of the Manichees, boldly conjectures"

sides: Peter: "iidem sunt Pauliciani et Manichaei" (PETER l.783-785); Theophanes the Confessor already uses the name (THEO l.89626); Rački places them in one dualist line with Bogomils and Cathars (RACKI l.975-990)
Gieseler: Peter is mistaken (PETER l.3880-3881); Peter's own report that they condemn Mani (PETER l.959-961)

contested_claims.claim: Who borrowed from whom, Peter or Photius
sides: Gieseler, siding with Engelhardt: Peter followed Photius, throughout (PETER l.260-275, l.303-327); Rački: Photius wrote a few years before Peter (RACKI l.862-863)
Montfaucon: most of Photius's book taken from Peter; Wolf: Peter followed Photius only on the old Manichaeans (PETER l.265-271)

contested_claims.claim: Whether Peter of Sicily is Peter, bishop of Argos
sides: The Latin title by Blanditius (PETER l.250-252)
Gieseler: Blanditius inserted "Siculus"; the Greek and the Life of Peter of Argos (PETER l.252-258)

contested_claims.claim: Why the archbishop is not named
